messages.author: 74d76925a922fb10
messages.subject: RPostgreSQL won't deploy to ShinyApps.IO
parts:
Hello - Please Help! 

My version of RPostgreSQL won't deploy to ShinyApps.IO:
Preparing to deploy application...DONE
Uploading application bundle...Error: 
* Unable to deploy package dependency 'RPostgreSQL'
  
  The package was installed locally from source. Only packages
  installed from CRAN, BioConductor and GitHub are supported.
Execution halted

The reason that it wasn't installed from CRAN is that it is incompatible with R3.1.2 and results in this error message when attempting to install from CRAN:
In file included from RS-PQescape.c:7:
./RS-PostgreSQL.h:23:14: fatal error: 'libpq-fe.h' file not found
#    include "libpq-fe.h"
             ^
1 error generated.
make: *** [RS-PQescape.o] Error 1
ERROR: compilation failed for package ‘RPostgreSQL’ 

So the work-around is to download locally and install the package as source, but then the problem is that it won't deploy to ShinyApps.IO.
CATCH-22
 
If it makes a difference, I'm on OSX 10.9.5

Can anyone provide some help/guidance?

Thanks,
Isaac

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: RPostgreSQL won't deploy to ShinyApps.IO
parts:
Just so we're clear... this is not the type you normally want to use. Your type defaults to "mac.binary.mavericks", which means "Mac OS X Mavericks binaries". The "mac.binary" type means "Mac OS X Snow Leopard binaries". It's only because CRAN doesn't have Mavericks binaries for RPostgreSQL, and we happen to know that the Snow Leopard binaries do work, that makes this OK to do in this instance.

(Also, I was confused by your original email because you said you were installing from source--you weren't. You were downloading the Snow Leopard binary build and installing it, there was no source compiling happening. When repos=NULL, then type is mostly ignored.)

On Thu, Feb 19, 2015 at 10:56 AM, Isaac Wyatt <is...@newrelic.com> wrote:
Joe - that is amazing! Works perfectly.

I'm really embarrassed that I didn't know about that 'type' property. I guess I need to read up on what that does and when I should use it.

Best,
Isaac

Can you try this?
